summary: A Sporting News explainer on the history of the ODI Men's Cricket World Cup ahead of the 2023 edition in India (October 5 to November 19). It covers the first tournament in 1975, the full list of winners and finals, Australia's record of five titles, and landmark changes such as 50-over matches, coloured kits and the white ball. It also notes the controversial 1996 semi-final, the one-off three-year gap before 1999, and India's 2011 hosting and win.
one_line: Overview of Cricket World Cup history from 1975 to 2019, including winners, format changes and landmark moments, ahead of the 2023 tournament in India.
key_facts: The 2023 ODI Men's Cricket World Cup is held in India from October 5 to November 19 and is organised every four years by the International Cricket Council (ICC).
England hosted the first ODI World Cup in 1975 and also the following three editions; it was played in cricket whites with a red ball.
Eight teams played in 1975, including a composite team from East Africa; South Africa was banned from international sport because of Apartheid.
West Indies won the first World Cup in 1975 (by 17 runs over Australia) and defended the title in 1979, beating England by 92 runs.
India won its first World Cup in 1983 by beating the West Indies by 43 runs in the final.
Australia are the most successful nation with 5 titles (1987, 1999, 2003, 2007, 2015); India and West Indies have 2 each; England (2019), Sri Lanka (1996) and Pakistan (1992) have 1 each.
The 1987 tournament moved to the Indian subcontinent (India & Pakistan) and cut matches from 60 to 50 overs because of shorter daylight hours in Asia; Australia beat England by seven runs.

The 1992 World Cup in Australia and New Zealand introduced coloured kits, the white ball, fielding rule changes and day/night matches, and was South Africa's first after Apartheid ended; Pakistan beat England in the final.
In the 1996 semi-final at Eden Gardens, Kolkata, an unruly crowd protested India's poor performance and Sri Lanka was awarded the match by default; Sri Lanka went on to win the title.
The ICC tried a three-year gap between events after 1996, but it proved unpopular and 1999 in England was the only tournament to follow it.
India last hosted in 2011 as co-host with Sri Lanka and Bangladesh; Pakistan was barred from hosting after terrorist attacks on the Sri Lankan team touring the country.
In 2011 Pakistan ended Australia's unbeaten run of 35 World Cup matches, and India became the first country to win a World Cup at home by beating Sri Lanka in the final.
The 2019 final in England and Wales was won by England over New Zealand on boundary count after a Super Over.
